subject: Model fit eval — PayGrid parity discussion and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paygrid.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + recommended next steps: PayGrid model-fit eval

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we discussed and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

- Goal: Validate whether a selection of open-source models (quantized where appropriate) can reach parity with PayGrid's current proprietary baseline on your invoice-categorization & entity-extraction tasks.
- Success criteria (what you said): match or exceed baseline F1 on key entities within a 3% absolute delta, and no perceived regression on edge-case prompts during a 2-week POC.
- Data: you will share a 2k example prompt set (anonymized) + holdout labels; procurement/contracting needs to be in place before we exchange full data.
- Proposed models to evaluate (first pass): Llama 2 13B - QLoRA, Falcon-40B-Instruct (8-bit), and Redwood-optimized Vicuna-13B Q4_K_SF. We’ll run both accuracy and hallucination/regression checks.
- Deliverables: 1) prompt set + eval script (we provide), 2) evaluation report comparing open models vs your proprietary baseline (accuracy, hallucination rate, latency at 95th pct, token cost), 3) recommended rollout plan with fallback.
- Timeline: initial eval (2 weeks), deeper parity tuning (1 week), then POC integration if you want to proceed.

Attached: paygrid_eval_promptset_v1.csv (template), redwood_model_recommendations.md (high-level). I also linked the eval dashboard: https://redwood.app/drive/paygrid/evals/PG-2026-045

Next steps for us:
- You: confirm acceptance thresholds (you mentioned 3% absolute on F1) + send anonymized sample by EOD Thu 7/30 if possible.
- Us: we'll run the first-pass eval and share results within two weeks of receiving data.

If that all looks right, we’ll queue engineering to allocate a small dedicated GPU slot for deterministic runs and keep you updated on costs.

Thanks,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

---
Attachments: paygrid_eval_promptset_v1.csv, redwood_model_recommendations.md

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paygrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@paygrid.com>, Procurement <procurement@paygrid.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + recommended next steps: PayGrid model-fit eval

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Acceptance thresholds: we confirmed internally that a <=3% absolute drop in entity F1 is acceptable for going forward, but only if hallucination rates (false positives on critical entities like billing_account) do not increase by >1.5%. If hallucinations increase beyond that, we’d treat it as regression.
- Baseline numbers (proprietary in-house model): entity F1 = 0.912 (macro on key entities), hallucination rate = 0.6% (on sampled validation set), 95p latency = 220ms (on our infra). These are the targets.
- Sample: attaching an anonymized 2k sample next message (we’ll upload to the S3 staging link after procurement).

Request: can you also include the prompt set and exact metrics you’ll report (we need precision/recall/F1 per-entity, hallucination count, and a small QA checklist for edge cases)? Also want to see token-cost burn estimates for each model at parity.

One more internal ask — our security team will want to see quantization/regression risks and whether you have an automated rollback/fallback if quality drops in production.

If those items are in scope, happy to move forward with sending the sample once Procurement signs the SOW.

—Alex
Head of ML Product | PayGrid
alex.johnson@paygrid.com | +1 (415) 555-2444

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paygrid.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + recommended next steps: PayGrid model-fit eval

Thanks Alex — all good notes. We’ll include the metrics you requested and a QA checklist. Summary of what we’re attaching in this thread:

- paygrid_eval_promptset_v1.csv — prompt template + sample anonymized rows (you can replace with your 2k).
- paygrid_eval_results_open_vs_proprietary.pdf — we’ll populate after the first run; attached here is an example report from a prior customer so you can see the format and the per-entity breakdown.
- redwood_model_recommendations.md — detailed guidance on which model variants to try first and why (latency/cost/quality tradeoffs).

Quick answers to your questions:
- Metrics reported: precision/recall/F1 per-entity, macro-avg F1, hallucination rate (count + %), token-cost estimate (USD per 1k responses at median sequence length), and latency P50/P95 measured on our deterministic infra.
- Rollback/fallback: we support canary rollouts + automatic fallback to your proprietary baseline if production-quality signals (we’ll instrument prompt-level scores and drift detectors) cross thresholds. We’ll document the SLO for automatic rollback in the POC runbook.

We’ll also include a small set of edge-case prompts to stress hallucination behavior — those are in the promptset file. Once Procurement confirms the SOW link (cc’d), we can accept the staged S3 upload.

Next: We’ll start the eval within 48 hours of receiving the sample and procurement approval. Expect an initial report within 10 business days after we begin.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paygrid.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Recap + recommended next steps: PayGrid model-fit eval (tech notes)

Adding a couple of technical notes from the runtime/ops side so expectations are clear:

- Quantization / parity: In our experience a Q4_K or 8-bit quantization on the candidate 13B family yields ~1-2% absolute drop in F1 on extraction tasks in worst cases; Falcon-40B shows higher memory footprint but often better zero-shot instruction following. We’ll benchmark both accuracy and stability across prompt permutations.
- Latency targets: we’ll aim for P95 <= 300ms on our dedicated-run configuration for the 13B quantized variants. Falcon-40B-instruct quantized will likely be in the 350-450ms range; if latency is a hard requirement we can prioritize the smaller variants.
- Batch sizing & cost: we’ll provide token-cost estimates at batch sizes typical for your traffic shape (you mentioned many short requests). Continuous batching is less effective for short, high-concurrency requests — expect higher per-token costs; we’ll surface precise numbers in the report.
- Regression detection: recommend instrumenting prompt-level confidence + periodic held-out evals. If we see a >3% drop in macro F1 or >1.5% absolute increase in hallucination rate in production compared to the POC baseline, we trigger an automated rollback to your baseline model.

I’ll run the deterministic eval infra and upload raw logs + metrics to the Drive link so you can audit.

-Aditya
Sr. Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Appreciate the detail — this looks good to us. Two quick asks before we move the sample: 

1) Procurement needs a draft SOW + estimated costs for the 2-week eval + follow-up POC. Can you send a simple SOW and an indicative cost range? (Procurement cc’d.)
2) Security wants a short note on PII handling and whether you can run the eval in a VPC/private mode for the POC.

Assuming we get the SOW and the security note this week, procurement will push the staging S3 link and we’ll aim to have the sample uploaded by next Tue. If the first-pass shows parity within the thresholds you outlined, we’ll schedule an on-site integration POC the week after to test end-to-end latency on our infra.

Thanks — looking forward to the report.

—Alex
Head of ML Product | PayGrid
